Author: Sudhir Agarwal
Bench: Sudhir Agarwal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
Court No. - 34
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 2395 of 2000
Revisionist :- Brahmanand
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Revisionist :- K.M. Mishra, Anil Kumar Bajpai
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate

sentences.text:
Heard learned counsels for parties and perused the record.
2. This Criminal Revision under Section 401 read with Section 397 Cr.P.C. has been filed aggrieved by judgment and order dated 16.12.1999 passed by 1st Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Etawah in Case No. 396 of 1997 convicting and sentencing revisionist under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1954").
Thereagainst
accused-revisionist preferred Criminal Appeal No. 2 of 2000 which has been dismissed by 6th Additional Sessions Judge, Etawah vide judgment and order dated 03.11.2000.
This revision has been filed challenging both the aforesaid orders.
3. Learned counsel for revisionist contended that there was violation of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 inasmuch report of Public Analyst was not served upon revisionist.

* * "P.W-2,
R.S. Yadav, Food Inspector, has in his statement made mention of having sent the report by registered post to the accused on 18.03.1997.

He has clearly stated that since the report has not been received back with his office and the address mentioned in the receipt is the full address of the accused, in such a circumstance, the argument advanced by the learned counsel for accused that no compliance of Section 13(2) has been made, cannot be accepted."

(English Translation by Court)
5. This aspect has also been confirmed in appeal.
6.

However, I find that approach of Courts below with respect to compliance of Section 13(2) of Act is in the teeth of recent judgment of Supreme Court in Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019) (Arising out of S.L.P. (Criminal) No. 4314 of 2015) decided on 31.07.2019 wherein Court in para 15 of judgment said as under:
"The very purpose of furnishing such report is to enable the Accused to seek for reference to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis if the Accused is dissatisfied with the report.

entities.text: Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such safeguard provided to the Accused Under Section 13(2) of the Act is a valuable right.

In that view even if the despatch of the report on 07.04.1980 is taken as substantial compliance though it is beyond the period of 10 days from 18.03.1980 i.e., the date on which the prosecution was lodged, in the absence of there being proof of delivery of the report to the Accused; in the instant facts the valuable right available to the Accused/Appellant to seek for reference within the period of 10 days stands defeated.
In that circumstance when the Appellant/Accused is made to suffer the penal consequences, it will have to be construed strictly.

In the facts and circumstances of this case, since as already noticed above the report of the Analyst has not in fact been served on the Appellant and the mere despatch of the report as per the statement of PW-2 was not sufficient." (emphasis added)

7. Therefore, as a proposition of law, it cannot be doubted that prosecution, when challenged, must satisfy that notice issued under Section 13(2) has been served upon accused because it is right of accused and prosecution must prove that not only report of Public Analyst was sent by registered post, but it was actually served upon accused-Revisionist, which has not been done in the case in Brahmanand vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35014956/
2 hand.

8. In the result, this revision is allowed.
Impugned judgements and orders dated 16.12.1999 and 03.11.2000 are hereby set aside.
9. Certify this judgment to the lower Court immediately.
